title: BatchOps
description: INPUT of `dmtool batch <ops.json>` — a JSON array of independent verb invocations run in one process. Dispatch is stateless and non-transactional: every op is attempted, a failed child never rolls back an earlier write, and each result echoes its `id`/`verb`/`args` plus exact exit. The outer envelope has `outcome:completed` and `data.dispatched:true` after full dispatch; `data.allSucceeded`, outer `ok`, and the process exit report whether every child exited zero. A NONZERO CHILD IS NOT NECESSARILY A FAILED CHILD: a verdict verb (`rule check`, `model check`, `workspace check`) exits 1 when its verdict is negative, and a comparison exits 1 when it differs — both while reporting `ok:true`, because they ran. So classify a child by its own envelope (`ok` = did it run, `valid`/`data.matches` = what it found), never by its exit alone; the aggregate `summary` reports that split as `<n> of <m> exited nonzero (<f> failed, <v> reported a negative verdict or comparison)`. Optional `--observations <file>` overwrites the compact deterministic static-kernel artifact described by this response's `observationArtifact` annotation; observation mode preflights every child and accepts only caller-tagged rule-check conditions or computation add/modify specs in --dry-run mode. Observation mode keeps the same aggregate contract, and the nonzero-child rule above applies to it routinely rather than as an edge case: a candidate the kernel rejected is a nonzero child, so a capture containing an intentionally invalid negative control exits 1 by design. That is not a capture failure, and the artifact is complete and authoritative. Read the disposition off the envelope, not the exit: the capture succeeded exactly when `outcome` is `completed` with `written:true` (a preflight refusal is `outcome:rejected` and writes nothing; a failed artifact write is `outcome:error`, exit 70). Per child, the artifact separates the axes — `ok:true` with `valid:false` is a correctly rejected candidate, `ok:false` is a child that failed to run. Use `apply` instead for ordered, atomic edits to one model ({target,op,…}, one terminal gate + rollback — see `schema apply`).

verb.description: the verb to run (any except `batch`, which cannot nest)

args.description: the verb's argv (as on the command line, minus the verb)

id.description: optional caller tag, echoed back on the result for correlation; required and non-blank when --observations is used
